newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's foreign stock fund inflows rise in May.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's foreign stock fund inflows rise in May.

text.p: Funds flowing into South Korea for stock investment totalled $2.06 billion in May, up sharply from $680 million in April, the Bank of Korea said on Wednesday.

Of the total, funds brought in for direct stock investment rose to $1.87 billion in May against $600 million in April, while those for indirect stock investment, including money that flowed in through country funds and beneficiary certificates, amounted to $190 million, up from $80 million.
A bank statement said the expansion of the foreign stock ownership limit in May to 23 percent from 20 percent contributed to the fund rise.
During the first five months of this year, foreign fund inflows totalled $6.28 billion, against $6.7 billion a year earlier, the central bank said.
It said outflows of funds earned from stock sales were $790 million in May, resulting in the month's net fund inflows of $1.27 billion.
A total of $4.26 billion flowed out from the Seoul stock market in the first five months, against $3.87 billion a year ago, the bank said.
In the five-month period, net fund inflows were $2.02 billion.
